chapter: Teddy Wilson bands and Cafe Society
title: Teddy Wilson band sections and Hall's lack of road experience
summary: Shorty Baker, other brass and reeds, trombonist Jake Wiley and teacher Bobby Burns, and Hall never having travelled.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Anyway, So to get back to Teddy then, you were talking about Shorty Baker, that's what you were going to say. You called him, you had a name for him?
Why did you call him Hyphitz? Jascha Heifitz.
Because he sounds so pretty. He's a beautiful person. He was the backbone of the trumpet section and then we had Doc Cheatham, Karl George and , well, I already mentioned the reed section.
Stump Brady and there's the trombone player that I can't think of, he died.
And you said that Teddy would go around while he was with Benny and line up people?
There was a young white trombonist, Burns?
No, no. His father was Jake Wiley's teacher.
Right, Cas Tech, (phonetic) He was famous as a teacher. Cas Technical High School.
Well, see, I had never been to Detroit yet. I haven't been out west -- or any of those places. And the guys hated me for it.
Because I didn't have to travel on the road.
You didn't have to pay those dues.
No. Well, I paid them, you know.
